items.followUp: List the steps you would follow to develop a flowchart for calculating the average of three numbers.

rubric.why: A flowchart begins with a clear understanding of the problem to be solved.
rubric.description: State that the problem or objective must be understood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the problem/objective as the first requirement.

rubric.why: The required data and the expected result must be known before planning the flowchart.
rubric.description: Identify the inputs and outputs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning both input and output.

rubric.why: The operations and their order show how the inputs are transformed into the output.
rubric.description: Determine the processing steps and their sequence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the required operations or ordered steps.

rubric.why: Standard symbols and a check of the completed flowchart help ensure it is clear and correct.
rubric.description: Use standard symbols with arrows and check the flowchart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for drawing/checking the flow using standard symbols and flow lines.

modelAnswer: Understand the problem and clearly state the objective of the flowchart.
Identify the required input data and the expected output.
Determine the processing steps, decisions, and their correct sequence.
Represent the steps with standard flowchart symbols connected by arrows, then check the flowchart for correctness.

items.followUp: State two ways a user can protect personal information when using a computer system.

rubric.why: Computational systems may collect and store users' personal information, creating privacy concerns.
rubric.description: Explain the privacy concern of collecting or storing personal data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying personal information as data that may be collected or stored.

rubric.why: If access controls fail, private information can be exposed to people who should not see it.
rubric.description: Mention unauthorized access or exposure of data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing unauthorized access, disclosure, or a data leak.

rubric.why: Stolen or misused data can cause harm such as identity theft or fraud.
rubric.description: Describe a consequence of data misuse or theft.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant consequence such as identity theft, fraud, or misuse.

rubric.why: Security practices reduce the risk of unauthorized access and misuse.
rubric.description: Give a relevant protection measure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a measure such as strong passwords, access controls, or encryption.

modelAnswer: Computational systems may collect and store personal information, which raises concerns about users' privacy.
Weak security may allow unauthorized people to access or disclose this information.
Stolen or misused personal data can lead to identity theft, fraud, or other harm.
Strong passwords, access controls, and other security measures help protect personal information.

items.followUp: Name and sketch any two flowchart symbols other than the Start/Stop symbol.

rubric.why: The oval is a standard flowchart symbol for the beginning or end of a process.
rubric.description: Draw or identify the Start/Stop (terminal) symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a recognisable terminal symbol with its correct name.

rubric.why: The parallelogram is the standard symbol for input or output.
rubric.description: Draw or identify the Input/Output symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a recognisable parallelogram with its correct name.

modelAnswer: Draw an oval and label it “Start/Stop (Terminal)”.
Draw a parallelogram and label it “Input/Output”.

items.followUp: What is meant by the time complexity of an algorithm?

rubric.why: Efficiency describes how well an algorithm uses computing resources.
rubric.description: Define algorithm efficiency in terms of resource use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking efficiency to an algorithm's resource use or performance.

rubric.why: The main resources used to assess an algorithm's efficiency are execution time and memory space.
rubric.description: Name time and/or space as measures of efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning time and memory/space.

modelAnswer: Efficiency of an algorithm is how effectively it uses computer resources to solve a problem.
It is commonly measured by the time it takes to run and the memory space it requires.

items.followUp: Why is test data used when checking a program?

rubric.why: Test data is deliberately supplied to a program to examine its behaviour.
rubric.description: Define test data as data used to test a program or algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that test data is input used for testing.

rubric.why: The results from test data help check correctness and reveal errors.
rubric.description: State that test data checks results or finds errors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning verification of output or detection of errors.

modelAnswer: Test data is input data used to test a program or algorithm.
It is used to check whether the output is correct and to help find errors.

items.followUp: Write HTML tags that make text bold and italic, and show a short example.

rubric.why: A paired bold-formatting tag marks text to appear bold.
rubric.description: Give a correct bold formatting tag pair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct paired bold tag.

rubric.why: A paired italic-formatting tag marks text to appear italic.
rubric.description: Give a correct italic formatting tag pair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct paired italic tag.

modelAnswer: Bold text: Bold (also written as Bold).
Italic text: Italic (also written as Italic).

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the title element in an HTML document?

rubric.why: The head section is the part of an HTML document enclosed by the head tags.
rubric.description: Identify the head section and its tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly giving the <head> and </head> tags.

rubric.why: The head contains document information, including the title, which is generally not displayed as page content.
rubric.description: State what the head contains or where the title appears.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the title, metadata, or the title's appearance in the browser tab.

modelAnswer: The head section is written between the <head> and </head> tags in an HTML document.
It contains information about the document, such as its title and metadata; the title is shown in the browser tab rather than as page content.

rubric.why: Grouping bits in fours from the right gives 0011 0101 1111, with leading zeros added to complete the left group.
rubric.description: Group the binary digits into four-bit groups from the right.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct four-bit grouping, including leading zeros where needed.

rubric.why: The groups 0011, 0101, and 1111 correspond to hexadecimal digits 3, 5, and F.
rubric.description: Give the correct hexadecimal conversion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final answer (35F)₁₆.

modelAnswer: Group the bits from the right and add leading zeros: 0011 0101 1111.
Convert each group to hexadecimal: 0011 = 3, 0101 = 5, 1111 = F.
